story.title: Separate source claims from the conclusion before drafting
story.problem: Synthetic example. A bounded knowledge-work task produced a plausible first answer, but the result needed repeated corrections. The objective was to improve the usable outcome without hiding errors or relying on a more impressive-looking response. Inputs and acceptance criteria were fixed for this invented comparison.
story.change: The fictional contributor asked for a clear distinction between source claims, assumptions, and the final inference. The proposed next step is an independent source check on a new task using the same acceptance rubric.
story.result: No timed or scored follow-up has happened in this fictional story. The revised approach is a hypothesis, with no measured improvement or comparison percentile. There is enough information to propose an experiment, but not to claim that it worked.
story.lesson: When synthesizing conflicting evidence, keep the claims and your inference visibly distinct. Test whether a reviewer can trace important conclusions and identify unsupported assumptions before adopting the approach more widely.
story.limits: All events and numbers are fictional demonstrations of the reporting format. They are not customer evidence or a completed benchmark. A future real comparison must retain every trial, record model and evaluator conditions, and examine unseen tasks. This story is excluded from rankings, progress awards, and candidate discovery.
